decisions.reason: Having remained on the market into 2025, this safety shoe line appears to fit the firm's core protective-footwear knowledge and production system well, so management would be more likely to refine models than withdraw the line.

The comfort insole is closely related to the firm's footwear know-how and customer needs, but some risk remains that management rationalises overlapping insole variants if differentiation or sales are only moderate.

The supportive insole is still within the firm's absorptive capacity, yet among the insole launches it remains somewhat more exposed to portfolio consolidation if customer feedback does not justify a separate position.

The ergonomic safety shoe series is highly aligned with the firm's established design, certification, and manufacturing capabilities, and its continued presence suggests management sees enough learning and market acceptance to continue it.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialised but related extension of the firm's safety-footwear expertise, so they are likely to stay unless the niche market proves too small relative to the resources required.
As a flagship moulded insole tied to the firm's stated innovation direction, it strongly benefits from existing knowledge and ongoing learning, making withdrawal within the next year unlikely.
